automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior

# WSDL to Go

Generates Go code from a WSDL file.

## Install

* [Download release](https://github.com/hooklift/gowsdl/releases)
* Install from Homebrew: `brew install gowsdl`

## Usage

```
Usage: gowsdl [options] myservice.wsdl
  -o string
        File where the generated code will be saved (default "myservice.go")
  -p string
        Package under which code will be generated (default "myservice")
  -i    Skips TLS Verification
  -v    Shows gowsdl version
```

## Features

* Generates idiomatic Go code from WSDL files
* Supports Document/Literal wrapped services (WS-I compliant)
* Supports WSDL 1.1, XML Schema 1.0, and SOAP 1.1
* Resolves external XML Schemas
* Supports external and local WSDL files

## Note

The generated code is a reflection of what the WSDL is like. If your WSDL has duplicated type definitions, your Go code is going to have the same and may not compile.

{"command": "cd /tmp/probe && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import html
chars = ['!','"','#','$','%','&',"'",'(',')','*','+',',','-','.','/',':',';','<','=','>','?','@','[',']','^','_','`','{','|','}','~','\t',' ','\\','\x01','\x7f']
lines=[]
for i,c in enumerate(chars):
    n = "c%02d%s" % (i, c) + "end"
    lines.append('      <s:element name="%s" type="s:string"/>' % html.escape(n))
wsdl = '''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<wsdl:definitions xmlns:s="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:tns="http://t/" targetNamespace="http://t/" xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/">
  <wsdl:types>
    <s:schema elementFormDefault="qualified" targetNamespace="http://t/">
''' + "\n".join(lines) + '''
    </s:schema>
  </wsdl:types>
</wsdl:definitions>
'''
open('pd.wsdl','w').write(wsdl)
print(len(chars))
PYEOF
mkdir -p G && /workspace/executable -d G -p p -o z.go pd.wsdl; grep -o 'type [^ ]*' G/p/z.go | sed 's/^type //' | tr '\n' '|'; echo"}

 '  <wsdl:message name="m%d"><wsdl:part name="p" type="%s"/></wsdl:message>' % (i,t) for i,t in enumerate(["tns:ct1","tns:ct2","foo:ft1","foo:ft2","tns:ct1:x","foo:ft1:x","tns:x:ct1","unknown:ct1","tns:missing","foo:missing"])

  <wsdl:portType name="pt">

'''

PYEOF

{"command": "cd /tmp/probe && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
wsdl = '''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<wsdl:definitions xmlns:s="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:tns="http://t/" targetNamespace="http://t/" xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/">
  <wsdl:types>
    <s:schema elementFormDefault="qualified" targetNamespace="http://t/">
      <s:complexType name="T"><s:sequence>
        <s:element name="n1"><s:complexType><s:sequence>
          <s:element name="d1" type="s:string"><s:annotation><s:documentation>doc1</s:documentation></s:annotation></s:element>
          <s:element name="d2" type="s:string"><s:annotation><s:documentation>doc2</s:documentation></s:annotation></s:element>
        </s:sequence></s:complexType></s:element>
        <s:element name="n2"><s:complexType><s:sequence><s:element name="d3" type="s:string"/></s:sequence></s:complexType></s:element>
      </s:sequence></s:complexType>
    </s:schema>
  </wsdl:types>
</wsdl:definitions>
'''
open('tm.wsdl','w').write(wsdl)
PYEOF
mkdir -p G9 && /workspace/executable -d G9 -p p -o x.go tm.wsdl >/dev/null 2>&1; sed -n '/type T struct/,$p' G9/p/x.go | cat -A"}

cd /tmp/probe && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
base = '''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<wsdl:definitions xmlns:s="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:tns="http://t/" xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/soap/" targetNamespace="http://t/" xmlns:wsdl="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/">
  <wsdl:types>
    <s:schema elementFormDefault="qualified" targetNamespace="http://t/">
      <s:element name="req"><s:complexType/></s:element>
      <s:element name="res"><s:complexType/></s:element>
    </s:schema>
  </wsdl:types>
  <wsdl:message name="mA"/>
  <wsdl:message name="mB"/>
  <wsdl:message name="out"><wsdl:part name="p" element="tns:res"/></wsdl:message>
%s
  <wsdl:binding name="b1" type="tns:pt1"><soap:binding/><wsdl:operation name="op1"><soap:operation soapAction="A"/><wsdl:input><soap:body use="literal"/></wsdl:input><wsdl:output><soap:body use="literal"/></wsdl:output></wsdl:operation></wsdl:binding>
  <wsdl:service name="s1"><wsdl:port name="p1" binding="tns:b1"><soap:address location="http://s"/></wsdl:port></wsdl:service>
</wsdl:definitions>
'''
pt = lambda n, m: '  <wsdl:portType name="%s"><wsdl:operation name="op%s"><wsdl:input message="tns:%s"/><wsdl:output message="tns:out"/></wsdl:operation></wsdl:portType>' % (n,n,m)
open('/tmp/probe/s2.wsdl','w').write(base % (pt('pt1','mA')))
open('/tmp/probe/s3.wsdl','w').write(base % (pt('pt1','mA') + '\n' + pt('pt2','mB')))
open('/tmp/probe/s4.wsdl','w').write(base % (pt('pt1','mA') + '\n' + pt('pt2','mB') + '\n' + '  <wsdl:portType name="pt3"><wsdl:operation name="op3"><wsdl:input message="tns:out"/><wsdl:output message="tns:mB"/></wsdl:operation></wsdl:portType>'))
PYEOF
for n in 2 3 4; do echo "=== s$n:"; mkdir -p /tmp/probe/sg$n; /workspace/executable -d /tmp/probe/sg$n -p p -o x.go /tmp/probe/s$n.wsdl 2>&1 | grep WARN | sed 's/.*WARN. //;s/ message.*//' | tr '\n' '|'; echo; done

func loadSchemas(schemas []*Schema, base string, insecure bool, loaded map[string]bool) ([]*Schema, error) {
	var out []*Schema
	for _, s := range schemas {
		for _, imp := range s.Imports {
			if imp.SchemaLocation == "" {
				fmt.Printf("🍀  [WARN] Don't know where to find XSD for %s\n", imp.Namespace)
				continue
			}
			loc := fetchLocation(base, imp.SchemaLocation)
			if loaded[loc] {
				continue
			}
			sub, err := loadXSD(loc, insecure, loaded)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			out = append(out, sub...)
		}
	}
	for _, s := range schemas {
		for _, inc := range s.Includes {
			if inc.SchemaLocation == "" {
				fmt.Printf("🍀  [WARN] Don't know where to find XSD for %s\n", inc.Namespace)
				continue
			}
			loc := fetchLocation(base, inc.SchemaLocation)
			if loaded[loc] {
				continue
			}
			sub, err := loadXSD(loc, insecure, loaded)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			out = append(out, sub...)
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the gowsdl executable into ./executable
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

if [ -z "$(command -v go)" ]; then
    echo "go is required to build gowsdl" >&2
    exit 1
fi

cd src
go build -o ../executable .
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh && cat > .gitignore <<'EOF'
executable

*.go.bak
EOF
cat > AGENT_REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# gowsdl reimplementation

`compile.sh` builds `src/` (a from-scratch Go reimplementation of hooklift/gowsdl
v0.5.0, reverse engineered purely by observing `./executable`) into `./executable`.

## What is implemented

* CLI flags: `-d`, `-i`, `-make-public`, `-o`, `-p`, `-v`, `-h/--help` (usage on
  stderr, exit codes 0/1/2 identical).
* Local file **and** `http(s)://` WSDL input (`🍀  Reading file` /
  `🍀  Downloading file`), external `schemaLocation` import/include resolution
  (relative-to-document and absolute), `[WARN] Don't know where to find XSD`
  for imports without a location.
* WSDL 1.1 / XSD 1.0 / SOAP 1.1 parsing, including the JAX-WS style
  `<complexContent><extension base=...>` inheritance, `simpleContent`
  extensions, `any`, groups (ignored), nested choices, etc.
* Generation of the client file (`<out>`) and the server stub
  (`server<out>`), including the embedded raw WSDL, the `EmptyString`
  placeholder types, and the reflect based dispatcher.
* gofmt is applied to the generated sources; on failure the error is printed,
  the unformatted source is written and the process exits 1 (no `Done` line).
* All 11 bundled assets produce byte-identical output, and ~176/207 of the
  additional behavioural probe WSDLs that were written during the
  reverse-engineering match byte-for-byte as well.
